group_assessment.weighting: A computational meta-analysis of nine public bulk microarray datasets of human substantia nigra (70 control, 88 PD) with computational cell-type deconvolution. WWOX enters only through protein-interaction network centrality of the partners of 93 differentially expressed genes, not through any WWOX expression change. The observation (cell-composition correction removes most DEGs) is firm; the WWOX shortlisting is an interpretation of network topology.

multihop.note: The article cites no WWOX-directed reference that this reading could identify; reference list counted, not read.

entries.proposition: The study pools nine bulk microarray datasets of substantia nigra, 70 control and 88 PD transcriptomes.
entries.snippet: In total, 70 control (CTRL) and 88 PD transcriptomes were put together in our study.

entries.proposition: Correcting for neuron and oligodendrocyte proportions cuts the differentially expressed genes from 1050 to 93.
entries.snippet: With the second LMM, we detected a reduced number of DEGs (adjusted p-value < 0.05, FC > 1.2): 93 instead of the 1050 obtained with the cell proportion-unaware LMM (63 genes overlapping).

entries.proposition: No PD-causing gene and no gene proximal to a GWAS risk variant is among the differentially expressed genes.
entries.snippet: None of the PD-causing genes nor any of the genes proximal to GWAS risk variants were found among the DEGs.

entries.proposition: The interaction network is built from the direct interactors of the 93 DEGs, using experimentally validated interactions from six databases.
entries.snippet: For all databases, only experimentally validated interactions were selected

entries.proposition: Central proteins are defined by degree and betweenness centrality above the 95th percentile of that network.
entries.snippet: we identified 207 nodes that have both a degree centrality higher than the 95th percentile (288 nodes) and a betweenness centrality higher than the 95th percentile (288 nodes)

entries.proposition: WWOX is named once in the body, in a list of central proteins with 'compelling evidence' for a role in neurodegeneration, cited to two references; the paper reports no WWOX expression value.
entries.snippet: other hits with compelling evidence supporting their role in neurodegeneration (e.g., GSK3β, WWOX, and VPC) [77,78], corroborate that new potential players in the PD pathogenesis might be identified among the central proteins we found.

entries.proposition: The authors state that PD-causing genes, though not differentially expressed, are enriched in the network, which is how the network is justified.
entries.snippet: PD-causing genes and those proximal to GWAS variants, albeit not being differentially expressed, were enriched in this network.

entries.proposition: Many of the usually reported pathways (Parkinson disease, oxidative phosphorylation, alpha-synuclein) may be driven by cell composition rather than pathology.
entries.snippet: several of the usually reported pathways (e.g., Parkinson’s disease pathway, oxidative phosphorylation, alpha-synuclein pathway) might be driven, at least in part, by changes in cell composition rather than the pathological status

entries.proposition: Limitation: genotype and Braak stage could not be examined because sample annotation was incomplete.
entries.snippet: the incomplete annotation of the samples across the studies prevented us from exploring the effect of age, age of onset, pathology progression, genotype, and Braak staging
